name: Fruit size / caliber
summary: Berry weight or equatorial diameter -- a genetics- and management-driven attribute with strong commercial weight, and one prone to unmeasured marketing description.
what_is_it: Fruit size (or caliber) describes how large an individual berry is, typically reported as weight in grams or equatorial diameter in millimeters.
why_it_matters: Larger fruit commands a price premium in most retail channels, is generally easier and cheaper to hand-harvest per kilogram, and is a headline attribute in many variety launch announcements. It is one of the most consumer-visible quality signals at point of sale.
how_evaluated: Objective measurement is straightforward -- weighing a sample or measuring diameter -- but reporting is inconsistent across sources. Plant variety examination reports typically state a measured range; marketing terms such as 'jumbo' or 'extra-large' are descriptive claims, not standardized measurements, and do not map to a fixed size threshold across companies.
what_affects_it: Genetics sets the typical size range for a variety, but crop load (how many berries the plant is carrying), irrigation, nutrition, and thinning practices all shift realized fruit size within that range season to season.
how_to_interpret: Marketing terms such as 'jumbo' are owner claims, not measurements -- treat size descriptors from a company's own marketing separately from a measured weight or diameter figure from an independent trial or examination report. Two varieties both described as 'large' may differ meaningfully in actual grams or millimeters.
